title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 97-99 of the manuscript, numbered 48-50 by Grothendieck). This is a Longue Marche-era (1981) study of how sections of fundamental-group extensions relate to rational points. The set-up is as follows. K/k is a function field of one variable over a field k of characteristic 0. U_{K/k} is a hyperbolic curve over K. E_K is the arithmetic fundamental group of K (Gal(K^sep/K)). E_{U_K} is the extension 1 → π → E_{U_K} → E_K → 1, where π is the geometric fundamental group. A place s of K, or a point s of a model S, gives a decomposition subgroup E_{K_s} ⊂ E_K, defined up to conjugacy. Grothendieck restricts E_{U_K} to E_{K_s} and studies sections. Sections 'de première espèce' come from honest points (here f(s) ∈ N_s(k(s))). Sections 'de seconde espèce' are cuspidal: they normalize an inertia subgroup L_i ⊂ π at a puncture.

The page first finishes the dichotomy. If the section does not define a point s, one gets an action of the second kind normalizing some L_i in π, i.e. a cuspidal section.

It then says that so far only places of K/k where U_{K/k} has good reduction have been treated. That case was explicit, since one started from a smooth model 𝒰 over S. He now wants to leave this hypothesis ('ce qui se passe dans le cas où on sort de cette hypothèse'). The question is what kinds of actions of the local group E_{K_s} on π (through E_K) the previous construction yields at points s ∈ S of bad reduction.

The test case is k = Q, K the function field of a modular curve for (punctured) elliptic curves, and s a place at infinity (a cusp), corresponding to a degenerate elliptic curve. In modern terms this is the Tate curve over Q((q)).

The next page makes this precise. It works over a henselian trait S with residue field k, with a curve of type (1,1) on the generic fibre. E_η sits in 1 → T → E_η → E_k → 1 with T = Ẑ(1) the (tame) inertia. Grothendieck notes that T acts on π by a non-trivial outer action (the monodromy, a Dehn twist). He guesses that triviality of this action characterizes good reduction. Hence E_k does not act outerly on π, but every splitting of (30) gives an outer action.
errors: No mathematical error on this page. 'E_{K(s)}' should be read as the decomposition/local group E_{K_s} (henselisation or completion at s), not the Galois group of a residue field; the next page confirms this by passing to the henselisation of O_s.

ideas.what: Dichotomy for sections of π1 extensions over a local or decomposition group: either the section comes from a point ('première espèce'), or it normalizes an inertia subgroup L_i of a cusp ('deuxième espèce')
ideas.modern_name: Geometric vs cuspidal sections in the section conjecture; packets of cuspidal sections
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (letter to Faltings 1983); developed by Nakamura, Tamagawa, Stix ('cuspidal sections')
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings 1983 (section conjecture, cuspidal case implicit); Longue Marche partially edited by Malgoire 1995

ideas.what: Studying the Galois action on π1 of a curve at places of bad reduction, with the cusp of the modular curve (degenerate elliptic curve / Tate curve) as the model case
ideas.modern_name: Galois action on π1 of degenerating curves; Tate curve, tangential base points at cusps of moduli
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara, Deligne (1989 tangential base points), Nakamura, Ihara–Nakamura (1997), Asada
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions the modular tower and cusps, not this local computation

ideas.what: Guess (on the next page) that good reduction corresponds to trivial outer action of inertia on π, with non-trivial monodromy at bad reduction
ideas.modern_name: Oda's good reduction criterion (Oda 1990/95; Tamagawa 1997 for affine curves)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets out to classify the 'types d'actions' of the local decomposition group on π (via the section construction) at places of bad reduction. The modular curve's cusp is his test case. This is a programme for a local section conjecture at degenerate places, done earlier than the modern treatments of cuspidal and degenerate sections.
missed.quote: examiner quels types d'actions de E_{K(s)} sur E_K on obtient par la construction précédente, en les s ∈ S où on a "mauvaise réduction"
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This was later developed independently (Nakamura's degeneration methods, Stix's cuspidal sections, p-adic section conjecture work), so it is mainly of historical priority interest rather than an open thread.

deep.surprise_reason: The page shows an early (c. 1981) explicit plan to analyse sections and Galois actions on π1 at bad-reduction places, using the Tate curve at the cusp of the modular curve. Together with the next page it foreshadows Oda's criterion. These themes are now well developed by others, so it is a notable historical anticipation rather than new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: 'dans le cas où on s'en[?] — dans cette hypothèse' should read 'dans le cas où on sort de cette hypothèse'.
'(corps des fonctions valuées[?] d'une variable)' is likely '(corps de fonctions algébriques d'une variable)' or similar; 'valuées' is doubtful.
'E_{K(s)}' should be interpreted as the local group E_{K_s} (decomposition group at s).
'[-courbes elliptiques, ...-]{+ponctuées[?]+}' : the struck words begin with '(courbes ...' and the insertion appears to be 'pointées', not 'ponctuées' (uncertain).
'en partant[?] d'une 𝒰 sur S' probably reads 'en partant ici d'une 𝒰 sur S'.
